newsitem.title: UK: NWE oil products firm, gasoline up on tight supply.
newsitem.headline: NWE oil products firm, gasoline up on tight supply.

text.p: NWE oil products were firmer on Monday, traders said.
Gasoline was $2 or so stronger as tight supplies combined with strong U.S. numbers propelled barges to $186 fob and cargoes to $208 cif NWE.
Spot gas oil prices were $2-3 a tonne firmer with tighter Rotterdam supplies strengthening premiums to firmer benchmark IPE gas oil futures.
Outright trade was thin with a strong dollar versus the Deutschmark keeping demand from Germany quiet.
"The Germans are buying cheaper oil inland" one broker said.
A backlog of barges waiting to load at the jointly owned BP, Texaco Nerefco refinery in Rotterdam was also seen causing short-term supply problems, traders said.

High sulphur fuel oil barges rose by more than $1 to trade at $87.25 fob ARA on short covering, while low sulphur barges were inactive but assessed notionally lower at $94/$96 in the absence of demand.

High sulphur Russian cracked cargoes were offered at high prices but buyers were not seen at those levels and straight-run was still fetching steady premiums, with very low avails of M-40 and E-4 seen.
